skill.name: xget
skill.description: Configure Xget URL rewriting for package, container, download, and AI API acceleration using live platform data and helper scripts.
skill.summary: Rewrite upstream URLs and configuration to use an Xget deployment.
skill.author: xixu-me

security_audit.summary: Most script command-execution alerts are false positives from JavaScript template literals, and most placeholder URL alerts are benign documentation. Real risks remain because the skill fetches live remote guidance, encourages execution-first behavior, writes persistent shell profiles, and targets credential-bearing config files. Publication should require confirmation gates and stronger source-trust controls.

remediation.issue: Remote README and platform data can influence local edits.
remediation.suggestion: Pin remote sources to a reviewed commit or verify content digests before adapting guidance into files or commands.

remediation.issue: The workflow encourages direct execution and file modification.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running commands, changing project files, or applying live README snippets.

remediation.issue: Persistent shell profile setup writes to startup files.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer temporary environment variables unless the user explicitly asks for persistent shell configuration.

remediation.issue: Package manager and environment config files may contain credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Use targeted edits, redact secrets in output, and avoid printing full .env, .npmrc, or similar file contents.

remediation.issue: Custom source URLs can point the helper at untrusted content.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before using --source-url or --readme-url values outside the trusted Xget repository.

content.user_title: Accelerate Downloads and Registry URLs with Xget
content.value_statement: Developers spend time rewriting package, container, and API endpoints for Xget deployments. This skill fetches current Xget guidance and applies matching URL and configuration changes.
actual_capabilities: Resolve an Xget base URL from user input, command options, or XGET_BASE_URL.
Convert supported upstream URLs to Xget path prefixes using the live platform catalog.
Fetch README Use Cases sections and rewrite examples to a chosen base URL.
List supported platforms and matching README headings through the included Node helper.
Adapt Xget configuration for package managers, containers, CI/CD, and AI SDKs.
limitations: Requires network access to GitCode raw URLs for the latest platform map and README.
Can modify shell profiles or project configuration when the user requests execution.
Does not verify that a custom Xget deployment is reachable.
Live upstream content changes can alter generated guidance.

use_cases.title: Convert Project Download URLs
use_cases.description: Rewrite repository, release, or package URLs so a project can route downloads through an Xget deployment.

use_cases.title: Configure CI and Container Builds
use_cases.description: Apply Xget registry and download endpoints inside Dockerfiles, compose files, and automation workflows.

use_cases.title: Route AI SDK Requests
use_cases.description: Update SDK base URLs for supported inference providers while preserving existing authentication behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this upstream URL to my Xget base URL: [URL]. Use [BASE_URL] and explain the matched platform.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Package Manager
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this project to use Xget for [npm, pip, cargo, or another tool]. Inspect relevant config files and make minimal changes.

prompt_templates.title: Wire CI and Containers
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my Dockerfile and CI workflow to use Xget. Keep current build behavior and summarize the changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Repository Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository for download, registry, and AI SDK endpoints. Replace safe targets with my Xget deployment and list any risks.

output_examples.input: Convert a GitHub repository URL for a specific Xget base URL.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the GitHub platform and returns the equivalent Xget URL with the selected base.

output_examples.input: Set XGET_BASE_URL for a zsh environment.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms the shell, applies the requested environment setting, and notes that a new shell may be needed.

output_examples.input: Find Docker Compose guidance for Xget.
output_examples.output: The skill fetches the matching README section, rewrites public demo URLs to the chosen base URL, and summarizes required edits.

best_practices: Provide the real Xget base URL before requesting file or shell changes.
Review changes to files that can contain credentials before committing them.
Refresh the platform list before converting unfamiliar upstream URLs.
anti_patterns: Using xget.example.com in live commands or production configuration.
Applying persistent shell profile edits without confirming the target shell.
Copying whole live README sections when one focused subsection is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill configure?
faq.answer: It configures URL and endpoint changes that route supported tools through an Xget deployment.

faq.question: Does it need my Xget base URL?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the base URL for real changes, or use the placeholder only in documentation.

faq.question: Can it update existing project files?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to edit relevant project files when the user asks for implementation.

faq.question: Does it fetch live Xget documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. The included helper can fetch the current platform catalog and README use cases.

faq.question: Can it work without network access?
faq.answer: Only partially. Stable reference guidance remains available, but current platform data requires network access.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
